reviewType: Independent AI editorial and sampled primary-source review
conclusion: All 100 manuscript bodies were read. Twenty representative manuscripts were deeply compared with 40 unique physical primary-PDF pages, including checked and needs-review records. No blocking unsupported technical or numerical claim was identified in those samples. One minor wording change and one family-repetition advisory are recorded. Existing source ambiguities remain unresolved.

scope.selection: Purposive sample covering transmission electrical/hydraulic checks, DEF sensors/heaters/pressure, throttle, fuel adaptation, injector mappings, barometric input, oxygen-sensor diagnostics and ignition-driver mapping. Not a statistically random sample.
scope.method: Read all 100 technical bodies and source/scope metadata. Compare 20 selected manuscripts with actual cited text sections, including continuation pages. Inspect eight original PDF pages where row layout, polarity, labels or numbers needed confirmation. Hash current manuscript bytes after review.

findings.location: Description metadata and section A detail requiring source clarification
findings.finding: The manuscript calls the source timing wording inconsistent/contradictory. The original row does combine an on-state check with an LSO turn-off-time item, but this alone does not prove a contradiction: the timer may describe another part of the driver sequence.
findings.action: Prefer unresolved timing relationship (description) and timing wording requiring clarification (body) over inconsistent/contradictory. Keep needs-review until an applicable procedure or source clarification establishes the sequence.
findings.correction: Description and body now describe an unresolved timing relationship instead of asserting inconsistent or contradictory source wording.

findings.files: Injector-channel and related electrical-driver article families in batch-14
findings.finding: Several family articles reuse the same supply/enable-state, no-automatic-part-verdict, internal-node-versus-connector and unresolved-mapping cautions. The monitor rows genuinely share logic, so differing channel labels do not justify invented mechanical distinctions. The articles are more differentiated by channel, fault category and evidence than by unique repair paths.
findings.action: During final editing, shorten repeated cautions where they displace useful explanation. Add channel-specific harness/component guidance only after obtaining applicable primary service data. Do not manufacture differences or advertise these monitor summaries as complete vehicle-specific repair instructions.

limitations: This is an AI sample review, not mechanic certification, vehicle inspection or a safety/repair authorization.
The other 80 manuscripts received an editorial body read, not the same deep independent primary-source comparison as the 20 listed samples.
No model, engine, transmission or VIN fitment has been established from the unresolved GM application-matrix filename join.
Internal injector/coil identifiers are not assumed to equal physical cylinder or coil positions; a different label is not itself evidence of a manufacturer error.
Existing needs-review classifications are retained. No live vehicle tests, wiring-diagram verification, diagnostic-tool validation or external expert review were performed.
The review does not certify SEO usefulness, originality against the whole web, completeness of a repair procedure or eligibility for automatic publication.
Manuscripts and shared project files were not changed by this review.
